title: Staggered upgrade windows and tenant-score-based load shedding for private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: reduce blast radius during control-plane upgrades and regional incidents for Dedicated/Private customers by combining staggered control-plane upgrade windows, tenant scoring for graceful load shedding, and ephemeral circuit-breakers that trigger progressive KV-cache eviction and request throttles. Background: recent incident (2025-01-26) showed cross-tenant latency spikes during a simultaneous control-plane rollout in 3 regions. Current controls are binary (full-quarantine or pass-through) which causes abrupt customer-visible failures or excessive overprovisioning. Proposed solution: 1) Introduce tenant_score (operational score computed from recent error rate, p95 latency deviation, and traffic volatility) to drive an ordered degrade policy. 2) Implement staged rolling upgrades with per-tenant upgrade-windows and capacity reservations to protect tenants with high score. 3) Add ephemeral circuit-breaker service (sidecar) that tracks per-tenant token rates and short-term queue depth; breakers emit events to the control plane and trigger tiered actions: soft-throttle (5-20%), KV-cache eviction prioritizing low-utility prefixes, request prioritization, then hard-quarantine. 4) Expand Prometheus/Grafana dashboards for tenant_score, breaker trips, and SLO burn rates; add alerting rules for cross-tenant correlated SLO erosion. Success criteria: - No region-wide SLO breaches during staged upgrades in canary tests - 90% reduction in number of full tenant quarantines during incidents - Clear correlation between tenant_score thresholds and mitigation actions in runbooks - Rollout can be aborted and state reverted within 10 minutes Rollout plan: a) Spike (lab) tests with synthetic tenants and adjustable score weights b) Canary in non-prod control plane c) Small percentage (5%) of dedicated pools with read-only traffic for 48h d) Gradual ramp by tenant risk band e) Full rollout with telemetry gating and kill-switches Testing and validation: chaos experiments (network partitions, node drain), load tests at 3x baseline, controlled failures to validate breaker behaviour, and integration tests for KV eviction heuristics Observability and runbooks: link to runbook and dashboards below. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, request error rate, SLO burn rate per-tenant, breaker trip counts, KV cache hit ratio.
